jobs.title: Corporate & Integration Operations Associate
jobs.jd_full:
Remote role based in Athens, covering mostly US East Coast hours (afternoons and evenings in Athens). Independent contractor engagement at $3,500–$4,500 per month (USD), depending on experience. As a contractor, you’ll invoice us monthly and handle your own taxes and social security contributions.

ABOUT 3Y HEALTH

3Y Health is building the operating system for healthcare practices, an AI-native platform that helps clinicians start, run and grow their practice. We work as a managed services organization (MSO): along with the software, our operations team runs the back office for the clinics we partner with, including billing, insurance and compliance. We currently serve applied behavior analysis (ABA) therapy practices and are expanding into other specialties. We're backed by over $200mm from Founders Fund, General Catalyst, SoftBank and 8VC.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We enter new markets by acquiring a foundational clinic for each specialty and region we go into, and we partner with independent clinics across the country. Every clinic adds entities, filings, contracts, staff records and deadlines that need to stay in order.

In this role, you'll own a set of our entities from start to finish. When we acquire a clinic, you'll carry out its integration plan: collect and file the records, prepare the filings, get staff ready for day one and follow up with everyone until each item is closed. Each deal comes with a detailed plan and timeline from the deal lead. Acquired clinics keep running largely as they do today until we bring them onto our platform, usually within a few months. Once a clinic is integrated, you'll keep its entity in good standing, alongside the existing entities you own.

You don't need experience in US healthcare. Every deal comes with a detailed checklist, and we'll teach you the US specifics. You need to learn fast, care about details and follow through. You'll work closely with our Corporate Development, Legal, Billing and HR teams in the US, and with a teammate in the same role.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Acquisitions

  • Work through each deal's integration checklist from before signing through the first months after close, keep the tracker current, and flag anything at risk of slipping

  • Document how the clinic runs today, such as scheduling, intake, referrals and billing handoffs

  • Check that each acquired entity is in good standing, and that its legal name and tax ID match across IRS, state, bank and payer records

  • Support our team and advisors on payer change-of-ownership notices, Medicare enrollment updates and credentialing checks

  • Map every payer's electronic payment setup (EFT/ERA) and each clinic's bank accounts, so our billing team can keep cash flowing through close

  • Prepare staff for day one: verify the employee roster, gather employment records for legal review, run license and exclusion checks, collect onboarding paperwork securely, and help get payroll, benefits and staff FAQs ready

  • Inventory each clinic's vendors, software and logins, collect business associate agreements (BAAs) for legal review, and track which systems switch to ours at close, later or not at all

  • Follow through after close on staff communication, moving patients of departing providers to remaining clinicians, lease and facility license items, and the former owners' transition commitments

Entity management and corporate operations

  • Keep the entities you own in good standing, primarily by managing our vendors: prepare annual reports, state registrations, IRS updates and other filings, and track them to on-time filing with our legal team

  • Maintain entity records, including formation documents, officers, registered agents and ownership

  • Prepare and submit provider and facility enrollments with state Medicaid programs and other public payers, and track them to approval

  • Make sure incoming mail for your entities is logged, routed and acted on, especially anything with a deadline

  • Prepare contracts from templates, route them for signature, and keep our contract management system and renewal dates current

  • Note what worked and what didn't, so our checklists get better with each deal

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

  • 2–5 years in healthcare operations, practice management, credentialing or provider enrollment, or acquisition integration

  • A track record of managing many details and deadlines to completion

  • Comfort working with contracts, licenses and government forms. You read carefully and catch errors.

  • Strong spreadsheet skills, and quick to learn new systems

  • Excellent written and spoken English. Most of your work is with US teams, agencies and vendors, and most decisions happen in writing.

  • Comfort handling confidential information

  • High agency and low ego. You don't need to be chased, and you'll do the tedious work as carefully as the interesting work.

  • Based in Athens and able to work mostly US East Coast hours (afternoons and evenings in Athens)

NICE TO HAVE

  • Experience in US healthcare, insurance or another regulated industry

  • Experience working with US companies or customers

  • Experience with corporate filings, contract administration or compliance work

  • Daily use of AI tools such as Claude or ChatGPT to work faster

WHAT WE OFFER

  • A monthly fee of $3,500–$4,500 (USD), depending on experience

  • A long-term role at a venture-backed US company, working closely with leadership

  • Room to grow as we acquire more clinics and enter new specialties

ENGAGEMENT

This is a long-term independent contractor engagement with 3Y Health, not an employment contract. You'll need to be registered as a freelancer in Greece, or be willing to register before your start date. You'll be paid monthly in USD.

If you meet most of the requirements and the role interests you, we'd like to hear from you, even if you don't check every box.

jobs.title: Senior Growth Manager (Contract)
jobs.jd_full:
Reddit is a community of communities. It’s built on shared interests, passion, and trust, and is home to the most open and authentic conversations on the internet. Every day, Reddit users submit, vote, and comment on the topics they care most about. With 100,000+ active communities and approximately 130 million daily active unique visitors, Reddit is one of the internet’s largest sources of information. For more information, visit www.redditinc.com.

Working as a Senior Growth Manager supporting Reddit’s International Community team, you will develop and execute initiatives that strengthen Reddit’s user and community ecosystems in the US and across international markets.

This position is open to candidates based in the UK or the US - East Coast.

This is not a marketing role. You will identify high-impact growth opportunities, design and execute experiments, and develop successful interventions into repeatable models that can be applied across markets. Your work may include building and scaling communities, increasing the supply of relevant content and contributions, reaching underserved audiences, and strengthening Reddit’s user experience.

The role combines growth strategy, hands-on experimentation, data analysis, and cross-functional influence. You will work closely with Product, Data Science, Marketing, and Community teams while maintaining the autonomy and entrepreneurial mindset required to scale successful initiatives to other markets.

Responsibilities:

  • User & Community Growth Strategies: Establish and execute comprehensive strategies to grow the user base and nurture communities.
  • Growth Experimentation: Design and execute growth experiments aimed at addressing gaps in content supply, community density, contribution, discovery, engagement, and user growth. Apply a creative, entrepreneurial approach by testing ideas quickly, learning from results, and iterating accordingly.
  • Scaling and Repeatability: Translate successful experiments into repeatable playbooks, processes, and recommendations that can be applied across markets. Determine which elements can scale broadly, which require local adaptation, and what operational or product support is needed to unlock broader impact.
  • Data & Performance Analytics: Monitor key growth and ecosystem indicators, including DAU, contribution, content supply, community health, and retention. Analyze performance trends, identify risks and opportunities, and establish clear measurement frameworks for experiments and scaled programs.
  • Cross-functional Collaboration: Partner with various internal teams to provide insights, shape priorities, and scale growth initiatives. Build compelling evidence through experimentation to influence cross-functional investment and product development.

Required Qualifications:

    • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.
    • 7+ years of experience in user growth, product operations, or market expansion, with a demonstrated track record of executing growth initiatives at scale.
    • Strong entrepreneurial instincts, hands-on execution skills, and the ability to make progress independently in ambiguous or resource-constrained environments.
    • Data-driven and analytical mindset, with proficiency in Excel modeling, working knowledge of SQL, and experience creating scalable processes and automations.
    • Strong systems thinking, with the ability to distinguish between market-specific problems and growth opportunities that can be addressed through repeatable approaches.
    • Exceptional communication and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively and align cross-functional stakeholders across global teams.
    • Results-oriented mindset, strong attention to detail, and a bias toward execution.
    • Comfort balancing a portfolio of opportunities across the US and international markets and prioritizing based on potential impact, feasibility, and strategic relevance.

In select roles and locations, the interviews will be recorded, transcribed and summarized by artificial intelligence (AI). You will have the opportunity to opt out of recording, transcription and summarization prior to any scheduled interviews.

During the interview, we will collect the following categories of personal information: Identifiers, Professional and Employment-Related Information, Sensory Information (audio/video recording), and any other categories of personal information you choose to share with us. We will use this information to evaluate your application for employment or an independent contractor role, as applicable. We will not sell your personal information or disclose it to any third party for their marketing purposes. We will delete any recording of your interview promptly after making a hiring decision. jobs.title: Associate Director / Director of Product Management, Signatera Hematologic Oncology (Heme)
jobs.jd_full:
Position Summary:

Natera is a global leader in cell-free DNA testing, focused on changing the management of disease in reproductive health, oncology, and organ transplantation. Signatera is a personalized, tumor-informed test for molecular residual disease (MRD) assessment and surveillance monitoring in patients previously diagnosed with cancer.

The Associate Director / Director of Product Management, Signatera Heme will own the product strategy and roadmap for Signatera in hematologic malignancies, starting with multiple myeloma and lymphomas. This person will work in a highly matrixed environment with the Foresight BU, R&D, Lab Operations, Software Engineering, Medical Affairs, Marketing, Business Development, and Regulatory. The role combines product management, market entry as a laboratory developed test (LDT), evidence generation, analytics, and clinical trial product support, including trials run under IUO and IVD pathways.

Primary Responsibilities:

  • Develop and execute the Signatera product roadmap for hematologic malignancies, beginning with multiple myeloma and lymphomas (for example, DLBCL, follicular, mantle cell, and Hodgkin lymphoma) and extending to additional heme indications.
  • Lead market entry planning for Signatera in heme as a laboratory developed test (LDT), including clinical validation requirements, CLIA and state requirements, market access/reimbursement and payer considerations, and launch readiness with Lab Operations, Regulatory, Medical, commercial and Marketing.
  • Define product requirements for blood-based malignancies with R&D, Lab Operations, and Software Engineering, including assay, sample type, workflow, and reporting needs.
  • Lead product support for clinical trials using Signatera in heme, including IUO use in studies with pharma and academic partners, and the path toward IVD and regulated use.
  • Partner with Regulatory, Clinical, and Business Development on trial start-up, study requirements, and pharma and companion diagnostic opportunities.
  • Build product performance metrics and dashboards. Analyze test volume, adoption, ordering patterns, turnaround time, and retention. Use the results to prioritize improvements.
  • Partner with Medical Affairs and Clinical on evidence generation strategy and execution. Areas of collaboration include identifying clinical gaps, designing studies, working with investigators and trial partners, and planning publications and congress presentations.
  • Guide product development for Signatera Genome in heme, including whole genome sequencing technology, phased variants, and structural variants. Work with R&D and Bioinformatics to define how these features improve tumor tracking and MRD sensitivity in heme malignancies.
  • Conduct Voice of Customer interviews, market research, and competitive and market intelligence in hematologic oncology.
  • Engage with key opinion leaders, advisory boards, and congresses (for example, ASH, EHA, and ASCO). Gather insights to guide product decisions.
  • Work with Marketing on product positioning, launch plans, pricing, and key collateral.
  • Build business cases and financial models to support product initiatives.
  • Present strategy, progress, and data-driven recommendations to executive leadership.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in life sciences, statistics, engineering, or a related field. Advanced degree (MS, PhD, or MBA) preferred.
  • 5+ years (7+ preferred) of experience in product management, product marketing, or market analytics at a diagnostics, biotech, or pharmaceutical company.
  • Hematologic oncology experience is strongly preferred, especially multiple myeloma and lymphoma.
  • Working knowledge of oncology molecular testing, next-generation sequencing (NGS), and biomarkers, including NGS bioinformatic workflows (e.g., variant calling, filtering, and interpretation) and genomic data analysis. MRD experience preferred.
  • Experience with data analysis. SQL, Snowflake, or similar tools preferred.
  • Familiarity with a high complexity molecular laboratory, including cfDNA or plasma workflows, is a plus.
  • In depth knowledge of whole genome sequencing and variant types, including structural variants, single nucleotide variants, and phased variants, is preferred.
  • Experience with clinical trials. Experience in IUO and IVD regulated environments is required.
  • Experience bringing a molecular test to market as an LDT, including clinical validation and laboratory requirements.
  • Experience designing or supporting clinical evidence generation, such as clinical validation studies, retrospective studies, or prospective trials.
  • Prior KOL engagement and external customer facing experience preferred.
  • 30-40% travel for advisory boards, congresses, and customer meetings.

Knowledge, Skill, and Abilities:

Technical

  • Understanding of MRD in multiple myeloma and lymphomas, including how blood-based MRD testing fits withing current bone marrow and imaging-based MRD assessment paradigms.
  • Understanding of how somatic variants are detected in whole genome sequencing and how they support MRD tracking in heme tumors.
  • Understanding of LDT market entry requirements and the evidence needed for clinical adoption and payer coverage.
  • Ability to translate customer and clinical needs into clear product requirements.
  • Strong analytical skills. Able to build metrics, interpret data, and present findings.
  • Basic financial modeling skills.
  • Proficiency with MS Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.

Behavioral

  • Ability to lead without authority and influence cross-functional teams.
  • Strong written and oral communication skills and ability to function effectively in a highly matrixed cross functional environment.
  • Ability to explain complex topics simply (biomarkers, multiple indications, regulatory pathways).
  • Strong customer focus, including building relationships with thought leaders.
  • Strong organization and time management. Able to manage several projects at once and meet tight deadlines.
  • Flexibility between fast development and quality standards.
  • Clear written and verbal communication with senior leadership.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORK ENVIRONMENT

Duties are typically performed in a [remote home office / hybrid office] setting. This position requires the ability to use a computer keyboard, communicate over the telephone and computer, and read printed material. Duties may require working outside normal working hours (evenings and weekends) at times. While the position may be based anywhere in the United States, availability during Pacific time hours is required and site based presence in San Carlos CA, Boulder CO, or Austin TX is preferred.

Travel required for this position: 30-40% (advisory boards, congresses, customer meetings).

The pay range is listed and actual compensation packages are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications and specific office location. This may differ in other locations due to cost of labor considerations.

$180,300—$230,900 USD

OUR OPPORTUNITY

Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives.

The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management.

jobs.title: Director Of Product, Onboarding, Hardware & Supply Chain
jobs.jd_full:
Toast creates technology to help restaurants and local businesses succeed in a digital world, helping business owners operate, increase sales, engage customers, and keep employees happy.

Toast’s Customer onboarding, hardware orders and inventory flows run on business systems that our Supply Chain, Finance, Care, and Onboarding teams rely on every day. As Director of Product – Onboarding, Hardware & Supply Chain Systems, you will own the vision, roadmap, and outcomes for those systems as part of the Business Technology & Transformation (BTT) organization. You will lead a team of product managers and BSAs while acting as a strategic product partner to leaders in Supply Chain, Finance, Accounting, Care, Onboarding, and Customer Success Operations. You’ll also work hand in hand with upstream and downstream BTT teams and R&D, so data and processes flow cleanly end to end across Salesforce, NetSuite, and the platforms between them and deliver scalable, high-impact solutions that support Toast’s exponential growth.

A day in the life (Responsibilities)

Strategy & Leadership

  • Set the multi-year vision and roadmap for Onboarding, Hardware & Supply Chain systems, tied to company strategy and the priorities of Supply Chain, Finance, Care, and Onboarding leaders.
  • Build, coach, and grow a high-performing team of product managers and analysts including hiring, career development, and clear accountability for outcomes.
  • Partner with senior Supply Chain, Finance, Care, Onboarding, and Technology leadership to translate business needs into scalable system solutions.
  • Work with upstream and downstream BTT teams and R&D to align roadmaps, manage cross-team dependencies, and agree on who owns data and integrations across systems.
  • Establish the team’s product operating model: how work is in-taken, prioritized, planned, and communicated, using outcome-based goals (e.g., OKRs).
  • Drive strategy to build scalable processes that power and support exponential growth in hardware, supply chain, and customer support operations.

Product Ownership

  • Own the hardware order experience from order to fulfilment, inventory-related supply chain systems, 3PLs, Onboarding systems, and key master data infrastructure.
  • Maintain and manage the project funnel, driving prioritization across multiple functional streams spanning operational improvements and strategic initiatives.
  • Own and deliver outcomes for high-impact strategic initiatives from discovery and design through launch, adoption, and measured business results.
  • Drive enhancements, integrations, and automation to improve efficiency, accuracy, and user experience across Salesforce, Netsuite and related platforms.
  • Ensure successful adoption: releases are communicated, users are trained, and usage is tracked.

Implementation & Optimization

  • Lead evaluation and implementation of new supply chain, hardware, and customer support technologies and tools, including Salesforce, NetSuite and platform integrations across business and engineering systems; making clear build vs. buy vs. configure recommendations.
  • Oversee integrations across enterprise platforms (Finance, Accounting, Care, Onboarding, data warehouse, and related systems).
  • Organize ambiguous ideas and targets into detailed functional requirements, providing point-of-view feedback on prioritization and criticality based on deep business understanding.
  • Lead delivery of large implementations, migrations, and enhancements, managing scope, risk, and cross-team dependencies from design through rollout.

Stakeholder Engagement

  • Act as a trusted advisor to Supply Chain, Finance, Accounting, Care, Onboarding, and Customer Success Operations leaders; bringing a clear point of view on priorities, trade-offs, and what’s technically feasible.
  • Build strong working relationships with engineering, R&D, and BTT partners to resolve cross-team dependencies and keep delivery moving.
  • Communicate roadmap, progress, and risks clearly to executives and stakeholders at the right level of detail, in both business and technical terms.
  • Translate business requirements into clear, actionable functional and technical specifications, and facilitate timely decision-making across a broad network of stakeholders.
  • Gather regular feedback from the people who use these systems (Care agents, Onboarding consultants, Supply Chain and Finance users) and use it to guide improvements.

Performance & Risk Management

  • Establish KPIs to track system adoption, stability, efficiency, and business results achieved through solution implementation (for example, order accuracy, on-time hardware delivery, inventory discrepancy rate, and time to onboard).
  • Proactively identify and manage risks in hardware, supply chain, Onboarding and customer support systems with clear mitigation plans and escalation paths.
  • Apply root cause analysis and systems design methodologies to resolve inventory discrepancies, hardware delivery failures, and process gaps, using a data-driven approach to problem-solving.

What you'll need to thrive (Requirements)

  • 10+ years of experience in Product Management, Business systems, or Supply Chain/Enterprise Systems, including system implementation, platform integration, and transformation.
  • 5+ years in leadership roles with proven ability to build and lead high-performing teams.
  • Experience with Salesforce, NetSuite, TMS/3PLs and Order Management systems required.
  • Demonstrated skill in systems analysis, including root cause analysis and process modeling/systems design methodologies.
  • Proven experience driving large-scale supply chain, hardware, or enterprise system implementations, migrations, or enhancements.
  • Proficient in how applications share data and communicate; expert in how data flows across systems, with the ability to articulate simple and accurate solutions to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Exceptional stakeholder management, influence, and negotiation skills, with the ability to build relationships with key executives.

Preferred Skills

  • Experience with customer support platforms (Salesforce Service Cloud, Amazon Connect, etc.) preferred.
  • Experience in high-growth, global companies.
  • Experience with vendor management, contract negotiation, and budget ownership for enterprise platforms.
  • Experience with 3PL/logistics partners, returns (RMA) or asset management.
  • Familiarity with emerging technologies in supply chain and hardware operations (AI/ML, automation, analytics tools).
  • Track record of success presenting to senior executives.
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

Success Profile

  • Strategic leader who sets a clear vision and roadmap for Onboarding, Hardware & Supply Chain systems, and delivers measurable business results.
  • Trusted partner to Supply Chain, Finance, Care, and Onboarding leadership; and to upstream and downstream BTT teams.
  • A leader who builds and develops a high-performing product team with strong delivery habits.
  • Change agent who drives operational transformation across hardware, supply chain, and customer support systems.

jobs.jd_full:
At Teamworks, we build the operating system for elite sports organizations, from D1 college football programs to professional franchises across the NFL, NBA, MLB, and NHL. Our Coaching and Personnel products sit at the heart of how teams identify, develop, and manage talent, and right now we're at an inflection point. Several acquisitions have put us in position to build something no one else in this market can: a unified, AI-first platform that connects coaching workflows, talent acquisition, and on-field performance analytics into a single operating layer for elite sports.

We’re hiring a Director of Product to own this product line. This person will lead a team of PMs and product leaders across our Football and Hockey products, own the roadmap for Coaching, Player Personnel, Recruiting, and AI in those two sports, and be a driver of innovation across our customers, partners, and leagues.

The Role

  • Own the product strategy and roadmap across coaching, scouting and recruiting products, across Football and Hockey. You’ll be responsible for driving coherence across a portfolio built through both organic development and acquisition

  • Define a cohesive, opinionated AI strategy that travels across your products. Identify the shared workflows (opponent scouting, self-scouting, talent evaluation, recruiting operations, free agency and the transfer portal, contract and scholarship decisioning) where AI agents create the most leverage, and turn that thesis into a multi-quarter roadmap

  • Lead and develop a team of product managers operating across multiple sports markets and geographies

  • Drive cross-functional alignment across engineering, design, data science, product marketing, GTM, and finance to move fast and ship product that wins in market

  • Stay relentlessly close to customers: front offices, coaches, coordinators, GMs, scouting directors, and league operators

  • Partner with Data Science, Engineering, and the PFF, SportLogiq, Zelus, and platform data teams to convert data products and proprietary models into deliberate calls on which capabilities are platform-level versus product-specific.

  • Find the workflows that look the same in front offices and the workflows where the two markets genuinely diverge, building a portfolio approach that maximizes shared platform leverage without forcing one sport's mental model onto another

  • Be accountable to revenue targets for the category, partnering with GTM to win league-wide deals and expand across football and hockey leagues and into international markets

What I'm Looking For

What You Must Bring

  • A track record of shipping and iterating across a multi-product portfolio: not just owning one product, but driving strategy and execution across several simultaneously. This is core to the role and non-negotiable

  • AI proficiency and the ability to build via a modern ADLC: a strong, current point of view on where agentic AI experiences win and where traditional SaaS workflows still serve users better, and the technical fluency to partner with engineering and data science to design and ship them.

  • Sports fluency: a deep understanding of how sports operate, enabling you to sit down with a GM, coach, or personnel director and credibly speak their language. This can come from many places: a genuine passion for sports that includes following the ins and outs of a given league, time spent in a front office, or experience competing as an athlete at a high level

  • Demonstrated experience leading PMs and product leaders through complex, multi-market environments (including through periods of organizational change like acquisitions or rapid growth), OR operating as a General Manager of a new business unit with full ownership of strategy, roadmap, GTM, and P&L outcomes

  • 8+ years in product management or software development within B2B SaaS, sports technology, vertical AI, or comparable industries

  • The communication and stakeholder management skills to operate credibly at the executive level, with customers and league partners, and with technical and GTM teams, all in the same week

Even Better If

  • You've built and sold product directly to professional sports teams and understand the buying dynamics at that level

  • You have subject matter expertise in football or hockey, whether from coaching, scouting, front office, analytics, or product work in those markets

  • You've shipped AI-native features (not just AI-adjacent, but workflows where the AI is the product), with direct experience working with proprietary data sets and the models built on top of them, including the tradeoffs between in-house ML, third-party foundation models, and hybrid approaches

  • You have experience working in recently acquired or integrating product portfolios, with a bias toward action and clarity in ambiguous environments

Why This Role

There is not a better seat in sports technology right now. Teamworks has the data, the team, and the customer relationships to become the definitive AI platform for elite sports organizations, and this role sits at the center of that build. 100% of the NFL, NHL, and Division I college athletic departments are all Teamworks customers. If you want to work directly these front offices while shaping a the future of a product category that doesn't exist yet in its full form, this is the role for you.

Human Interest is on a mission to ensure that people in all lines of work have access to retirement benefits. 

More than half of all working Americans are not saving enough for their future. Too often, it’s because they are employed by a company that doesn’t offer a retirement plan. About the role

Product management is changing. The best product managers no longer just write requirements and wait for engineering; they prototype their own ideas, pressure-test them with data, and use AI to move from problem to validated solution in days rather than quarters. We are looking for product managers who have embraced that shift and who want to apply it to one of the biggest unsolved problems in America: helping working people save for retirement.

You will independently own whole projects, each made up of multiple features, within a product area. You will turn the broader product vision into concrete plans your engineering team can deliver, and partner closely with Engineering, Design, Operations, Customer Success, and Compliance to ship accurate, reliable work that achieves the results it was meant to. You will do this as an AI-augmented builder: using modern AI tooling both to sharpen how you work and to help shape products that increasingly work on our customers’ behalf.

What you get to do every day

  • Own multi-feature projects end to end, from discovery through launch and iteration. Translate the broader vision for your product area into concrete feature plans, and give your team a clear picture of the customer experience you’re building.
  • Prioritize work based on expected customer and business impact. Define clear success metrics aligned with long-term goals, and report on outcomes, not just completion of tasks.
  • Notice when something you shipped isn’t achieving the desired results, dig into why, and recommend changes.
  • Produce clear requirements and artifacts that unblock engineering to deliver high-quality work on time, with accuracy and auditability built in.
  • Ensure your projects meet compliance standards, and create processes to validate data accuracy within your product area.
  • Develop deep knowledge of customer problems in your area. Combine qualitative feedback and quantitative data to represent user needs and anticipate requirements beyond what customers explicitly ask for.
  • Communicate effectively with engineering, design, and partner teams, manage tradeoffs and timelines within your projects, and explain complex concepts in simple, accessible terms.

How you work with AI

We expect our product managers to use AI to work smarter and solve problems faster, and to bring good judgment about where AI belongs in the product itself.

  • Prototype rapidly. Use tools such as Figma Make, Claude Code, Codex, or similar to explore, validate, and demonstrate ideas yourself, so you can align your team on direction with a working artifact rather than a document.

jobs.title: Lead Product Manager, New Customer Experience
jobs.jd_full:
About LawnStarter

LawnStarter is the nation’s leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, with over $750M in bookings. We’re expanding beyond lawn care to become the one-stop shop for home services: three brands (LawnStarter, Lawn Love, Home Gnome), one shared platform.

About Product at LawnStarter

Our BHAG: 1+ job per household, every year. Getting there means winning on four fronts at once: more customers, more Pros, excellent service for both sides, and an AI-run company that moves faster than its size should allow.

About the First Service Experience at LawnStarter

Every new customer meets us the same way. They land on our home page or marketing site, then move through a signup and booking flow where they get a quote, pick a service and a schedule, and pay. That flow runs across all three brands and brings in most of the company’s new customers.

We built it many years ago. It’s too long, and we lose customers at too many steps. So the real question isn’t how to remove a step. It’s whether the experience designed still makes sense at all, or whether it should be rethought entirely as an AI-native, agentic experience.

The Role

You’ll own the consumer’s first service experience: everything from the moment someone first encounters LawnStarter through signing up and booking their first service. You’ll decide what that experience should become, then build it with engineering, design, operations, marketing, and data.

This is not a funnel-optimization job. We want someone who looks at a five-year-old flow, asks what a homeowner would want if we started from nothing today, and then ships the answer.

As Lead PM, you’re an individual contributor with Lead-level scope and no direct reports. You’ll work closely with the Consumer Experience lead, the Pro Experience PM, the Pricing PM, and the Conversational AI & Agents lead. You’ll report to the Sr. Director of Product.

What makes this role different:

  • A rebuild, not a tune-up. You’re rethinking the experience from first principles, not polishing the one we have.
  • AI-native from the first screen. You’ll decide whether a form is even the right way to sign up anymore.
  • Every new customer passes through your work. Across three brands, this is how people meet LawnStarter.

What You’ll Own

  • The vision: What the first service experience should become, and the plan to get there.
  • The home page and marketing site: The first impression, and the first decision a customer makes about us.
  • Signup and booking for all three brands: LawnStarter, Lawn Love, and Home Gnome.
  • Funnel data: The numbers that show where customers move forward and where they leave.
  • Quotes, services, and scheduling: How a customer gets a price, picks a service, and chooses when it happens.
  • Payment: Checkout, including Apple Pay and Google Pay.

Problems to Solve

Deciding whether today’s experience should exist at all.
You’ll start from what a homeowner needs to book their first service and work backward. Every step we have today has to earn its place again, and you’ll defend each call with evidence.

Designing an AI-native, agentic way to sign up.
Someone who wants their lawn mowed shouldn’t have to learn our product to book it. What can an agent handle for them, and where does a person still want control? You’ll answer with prototypes in front of real customers, not opinions in a meeting.

Rebuilding without breaking what works.
This flow brings in most of our new customers. You’ll need a path that proves the new experience works with real customers before it replaces the old one. Bold and careful at once: that’s the job.

Moving levers you don’t own.
Signup touches pricing, Pro supply, and operations. Change how customers book and you change what Pros see and how jobs get priced. You’ll work through the people who own those levers and bring them along on a vision that changes their world too.

What Success Looks Like (Year 1)

  • A vision leadership rallies behind: A clear picture of the reimagined first service experience, grounded in what customers need.
  • A first piece of it, live: A meaningful part of that experience shipped to real customers. Not a deck.
  • Signup conversion goes up: More of the people who find us become customers.
  • More customers sign up for their first service: The reimagined experience gets more households to that first booking.

jobs.title: Lead Product Manager, AI Agents
jobs.jd_full:
About LawnStarter

LawnStarter is the nation’s leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, with over $750M in bookings. We’re expanding beyond lawn care to become the one-stop shop for home services: three brands (LawnStarter, Lawn Love, Home Gnome), one shared platform.

About Product at LawnStarter

Our BHAG: 1+ job per household, every year. Getting there means winning on four fronts at once: more customers, more Pros, excellent service for both sides, and an AI-run company that moves faster than its size should allow.

About AI Agents at LawnStarter

Our mission: power every AI experience. For homeowners and for Pros (the lawn care providers on our marketplace), conversational AI can do far more than answer questions. It can skip a service, reschedule a visit, or book a new one mid-conversation, even when the customer’s own AI agent is the one talking. And it doesn’t have to live only in a chat window: we’re bringing agentic experiences into the workflows homeowners and Pros already use, so the product does the work for them wherever they are. You’ll decide what that looks like for both sides, then ship it.

The Role

This is LawnStarter’s first core AI PM role. You’ll own our conversational AI and agent experiences for consumers and Pros: the chat, the actions it takes, the moment it hands off to a person, and how outside AI agents work with us. Beyond chat, you’ll bring agentic experiences into existing consumer and Pro workflows, so AI takes action inside the product rather than alongside it.

As Lead PM, you’re an individual contributor with Lead-level scope, reporting to the Sr. Director of Product. The AI experiences you power will often sit inside surfaces other PMs own, so you’ll share goals with the Customer Experience lead, the First Service Experience lead, and the Pro Experience PM, and build with engineering, applied science, design, data, customer service, and operations.

What makes this role different:

  • Fast, and at the center. Within a year, we expect AI to shape a meaningful share of how homeowners and Pros experience LawnStarter, and you’ll be at the center of making that happen. This role moves fast and rewards people who ship.
  • You’re the first. The evals, the guardrails, and the bar for “ready to ship” are yours to set.
  • The AI takes real actions. It reschedules and skips services on a live marketplace. No sandbox.
  • Two sides, one conversation. Everything you ship serves homeowners, Pros, or both, and an action for one changes the other’s day.

What You’ll Own

  • The AI roadmap: Where consumer AI and Pro AI go next, and the order we build it in.
  • Customer AI chat: Answering homeowners’ questions and completing tasks, like skipping or rescheduling a service.
  • AI chat in the Pros App: The AI experience Pros get inside the app they work from.
  • Agents inside existing workflows: AI that acts within the consumer and Pro flows people already use, not just in a chat window.
  • Customer-to-Pro messaging: How homeowners and Pros talk to each other.
  • The handoff to human support: When the bot passes a conversation to a support agent.
  • Outside AI agents: Letting a customer’s own agent, such as ChatGPT or Claude, work with us on their behalf.

Problems to Solve

From answering questions to solving problems.

A chatbot that explains how to reschedule is useful. One that understands what the customer or Pro actually needs, recommends the right thing, and then does it for them is a different product, and a riskier one. Sometimes the best answer isn’t the action they asked for: a skip might be better as a reschedule, or a one-time booking better as a plan. You’ll decide which actions the AI takes on its own, which need confirmation, and what happens when it gets one wrong.

Knowing when to hand off, and doing it well.
Some conversations belong with a person. Which ones? And can the bot tell before the customer gets frustrated? When the handoff comes, the support agent should pick up with full context so the customer doesn’t repeat themselves.

When the customer’s agent is the one asking.
Sometimes the one talking to LawnStarter won’t be a homeowner. It’ll be their own AI agent, such as ChatGPT, asking about a service, booking one, or changing it. You’ll work out what we let an outside agent do and how the customer stays in control.

Evals and guardrails for two audiences.
A good answer for a homeowner isn’t a good answer for a Pro. You’ll build the evals that tell us when an AI experience is good enough to ship and when its quality slips, plus the guardrails that keep it safe once it’s live.

What Success Looks Like (Year 1)

  • AI shaping the experience: AI experiences live for consumers and Pros, and shaping a meaningful share of how both sides interact with LawnStarter, measured by:

    • Share of conversations resolved by AI without a human (resolution or containment rate)
    • CSAT on AI conversations, for homeowners and Pros
    • Action accuracy: errors on reschedules, skips, and bookings stay below a set bar

  • Pros get more done because of AI: Pros spend less time on admin and coordination, and say AI makes them more productive.

  • More customers stay because AI makes service better: Consumer and Pro retention rises, driven by AI that resolves problems faster and improves the service experience.

Who You Are

Experience: 6+ years of product management, including at least 3 years launching AI products to customers (internal or external).

An AI builder who has shipped to real users. You’ve put AI products in front of real end users, whether in B2C, B2B, or B2B2C, and at least one was a chatbot or conversational AI running in production. You read transcripts to find where conversations break. If your AI work stopped at demos, prototypes, or a thin prompt wrapper that never met a real user, this isn’t your role.

The owner of quality. You write evals yourself. You know when an AI experience is good enough to ship, and when its quality starts to slip. Would you rather someone else define what “good” means? Then you’ll struggle here.

Fluent in agents and tool use. You understand what changes when an agent stops producing text and starts calling actions on real systems, and you design for the ways that goes wrong. PMs who treat AI as a feature bolted onto the side won’t last here.

A strategist who prioritizes with data. You set priorities, say no with reasons, and back each call with evidence. If your roadmaps run on instinct alone, this is unlikely to be a good fit.

A systems thinker. You see a product change as one part of a larger system and think through its second- and third-order effects before you ship. Here, that system is a marketplace: a change for customers almost always touches Pros, pricing, and operations too. You plan for those effects in the spec, not after launch. Marketplace experience helps, but what matters most is that you instinctively ask, “What else does this change?” If you’d rather ship your piece and let other teams deal with what it changes, this isn’t your role.

This Role Is NOT

  • A people-management role. You’re an individual contributor with no direct reports.
  • A research or ML-platform seat. If your AI career has been research or platform work that never reached end users, this isn’t the fit.
  • For AI skeptics. If you see AI as an add-on rather than the product, you’ll fight the job daily.
  • A strategy-only seat. You’ll write the evals and read the transcripts. Setting direction from a distance won’t work here.
  • A role with foundations already built. You’ll build the evals, the guardrails, and how we decide an AI experience is ready, not inherit them. We’re also lean and frugal, on a partly legacy stack.
  • Low-stakes. AI that reschedules or skips a service fails in front of customers and Pros, so the safety bar is high. And since your work lives inside surfaces other PMs own, you’ll lead through influence.

Bachelor’s degree in business, analytics, engineering, design, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience, plus 6+ years of product management experience on consumer-facing products.

  • Equity: AI is how LawnStarter plans to move faster than its size, and this role decides how that shows up for customers and Pros. Equity means you share in what that builds.
  • Base salary: $170,000 to $225,000
  • Healthcare: Medical, dental, and vision
  • Location: Fully remote (US). Evals, transcripts, and failure cases reward deep focus, and remote work protects it.
  • PTO: Flexible. We focus on results. Take what you need.
